output.brief: The buffering rise is almost certainly caused by the smart-TV app 5.2, not the new CDN. Version 5.2 went to 100% of Kestria on 9 Oct, the same day as the cutover. It cut the player's startup buffer from 10 s to 4 s. Rebuffering on 5.2 is about 5.9% on every ISP. Every other client is at 0.6–0.7% on the same Tessaline CDN and the same ISPs. Employee test TVs on the old CDN showed 5.7% before release. Handball demand and ISP congestion don't fit the pattern. So don't send the breach notice, withhold fees or move traffic back. That would punish the vendor and leave the problem in place. Don't mute the alert either; it is the only signal we have. Next steps: revert the Kestria abr_v2 setting to the 5.1 values (about an hour, no new build); hold the 20 Nov rollout to other markets until it's fixed; and add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard, with a manual query in the meantime. Hold the free-month offer. The link between buffering and cancellations is unproven, and the 1 Oct price rise is a competing explanation. Confidence is high on the cause and lower on cancellations.
